title: Edmund and the Salt
premise: Coral Iversen, a nonbinary archivist who keeps the ledgers of the Guild of Impossible Things, discovers their own name and tonight's date in a century-old book of prophecies — a book that predicts the erasure of Vessengard, a country that officially stopped existing forty years ago but survives behind a salt-sealed gate Coral guards. The prophecy names Coral as either the door's keeper or its key, and the guild's masked patrons begin arriving to claim them for one side or the other. To save the fading country and the found family of exiles within it, Coral must retrace their dead mother's final journey, recover three memories that were traded away before they were born, and open the gate from the inside — knowing that doing so will erase every memory anyone holds of Coral. In the end, Coral chooses to become the door itself: Vessengard endures, remembered by everyone except the one person who saved it, until a child of the guild finds Coral's ledger and writes their name back into the world.
about_author: Gideon Nystrom is the pen name of a former lighthouse keeper turned archivist who spent a decade cataloguing the papers of defunct trade guilds along the Baltic coast. Their fiction blends bureaucratic fantasy with quiet, aching meditations on what it costs to be remembered.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Tonight
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. During a routine inventory of the guild's vaults, Coral finds a prophecy written in 1899 that lists tonight's date, their own name, and the words 'the keeper becomes the key.' The emotional beat is dread disguised as professional calm; Coral's instinct is to file the page away and pretend it isn't real.

chapters.title: Salt on the Sill
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. The sealed gate beneath the guildhouse begins weeping brine, and the first masked patron arrives demanding access to 'the Vessengard asset.' Coral lies badly and realizes the guild has been guarding more than ledgers. Emotional beat: the vertigo of learning your whole life was a cover story.

chapters.title: A Country That Isn't There
chapters.summary: Coral's POV, with letters from their mother interspersed. Researching Vessengard, Coral finds maps that redraw themselves and learns their mother died inside the vanished country. Beat: grief sharpening into purpose — Coral decides to go through the gate rather than guard it.

chapters.title: The Guild of Impossible Things
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. The guild's inner circle convenes; half want Coral erased as a liability, half want them weaponized. Only Oddrun, the tea-brewer who raised Coral, defends them — and reveals she was born in Vessengard. Beat: betrayal and loyalty tangled together; Coral flees into the vaults.

chapters.title: Three Memories, Paid In Full
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. In the ledger of trades, Coral discovers their mother sold three of Coral's own memories before their birth to buy passage out of Vessengard. Beat: the ache of mourning something you never had, and the resolve to buy those memories back at any price.

chapters.title: The Ferryman's Price
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Bargaining with the guild's memory-broker, Coral trades their most precious possession — Oddrun's recipe book, full of shared years — to reclaim the first lost memory: their mother's face. Beat: bittersweet gain; each recovered memory makes Coral more legible to the prophecy.

chapters.title: What the Gate Remembers
chapters.summary: Coral's POV, shifting briefly to the gate's own consciousness. The second memory shows Coral standing at the gate as a child, already chosen. The patrons close in; Oddrun takes a blow meant for Coral. Beat: terror turning to fury; Coral opens the gate and steps into Vessengard.

chapters.title: Vessengard, Last Evening
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Inside, the country exists in a single repeating dusk, populated by the traded-away and forgotten. Coral meets the echo of their mother, who begs them to let the country fade peacefully. Beat: temptation of surrender versus the stubborn love of the people who refuse to disappear.

chapters.title: The Keeper Becomes the Key
chapters.summary: Climax. Multiple POVs — Coral, Oddrun, the patrons. The third memory reveals the prophecy's true choice: the gate demands a keeper bound to it forever. Coral accepts, unmaking themselves as an individual to hold the door open so Vessengard's people can cross into the world. Beat: sacrifice as belonging.

chapters.title: A Name Written Back
chapters.summary: Resolution, mostly Oddrun's POV. Vessengard's exiles rebuild in the world; no one remembers Coral — until a guild child finds a ledger where new entries appear in Coral's hand, and reads the name aloud. Somewhere, a door opens. Beat: grief transmuted into hope; memory as an act of love.
